subject.title: lossless-claw bootstraps into quarantine after every Gateway restart due to new sessionId generating fresh JSONL file

question: Should OpenClaw accept a default-off `session.restartContinuation` config that reuses aborted main-session ids across controlled Gateway restarts, or should restart transcript continuity be solved through a different core session-lifecycle rule?
rationale: The report is valid from current source, but accepting the proposed fix changes config surface and session reuse semantics, which repository policy treats as product and compatibility-sensitive.

options.title: Review and land the opt-in PR
options.body: Proceed with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/94567 if maintainers accept the new config surface and its upgrade-safety proof.

options.title: Require a no-new-config lifecycle fix
options.body: Ask for a replacement design that preserves restart transcript identity through existing session lifecycle rules instead of adding `session.restartContinuation`.

options.title: Defer to broader restart recovery
options.body: Keep this issue open under the broader Gateway restart recovery track if maintainers do not want a narrow LCM-driven session-id reuse knob now.

recommendation.title: Review and land the opt-in PR
recommendation.body: Proceed with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/94567 if maintainers accept the new config surface and its upgrade-safety proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main blame points this checkout's central session reuse and lifecycle guard code at Ben.Li, making them the best available routing candidate from local history for the product-sensitive session rule.
